processing: Downy shoots of one bud with one or two leaves are shaped flat and finished by a mix of pan-firing and baking, a half-roasted, half-baked green tea.
harvest_season: Spring, as usual for fine Hanzhong greens; the plucking standard is one bud with one or two downy leaves.
appearance_dry: Flat, shuttle-shaped leaves in a bright green, thickly covered with silvery down.
appearance_wet: Tender, plump buds and leaves in an even, bright yellow-green.
taste_profile: A fresh, mellow cup with a lasting young-leaf aroma, and a sweet return after the swallow.

brewing.notes: These are ordinary settings for a tender flat green rather than a local rule. Use a glass or an open gaiwan and leave the lid off so the leaf does not stew.

vintage_note: Like other Chinese greens, it is best bought as the current year's spring harvest and drunk within about a year. Earlier spring lots usually cost more. It does not improve with age, so an undated bag is a poor buy.
description:
Hanshui Yinsuo is a modern green tea from Nanzheng, in the Hanzhong basin of southern Shaanxi. The name describes it well: it grows on the upper Han River, and its flat, downy leaves are shaped like a weaver's shuttle and shine silver.

The shoots are chosen for plenty of down, one bud with one or two leaves. It is finished by part pan-firing and part baking, and the down stays visible on the finished leaf.

Expect a fresh, mellow cup with a lasting young-leaf aroma, then a sweet finish. As with other tender greens, too-hot water is the usual mistake: it flattens the aroma and pulls out bitterness.

It is sold as a spring green. Look for even shuttle shapes with clear down and ask for the harvest year. Sellers often quote long award lists and state-banquet claims, which say little about the bag in front of you.
history:
This is a recent creation of Nanzheng county, not an old tribute tea. It passed technical and quality assessment in 1986. Accounts of its national recognition give dates that do not fit together, including a Ministry of Agriculture title placed in 1982, so that date is best treated with caution.

Today it is counted among the Hanzhong teas that make up the wider Hanzhong Xianhao regional brand.
